Avoid continuous water stagnation at early stages.
Conserve natural enemies such as dragonflies, spiders, parasitic wasps, Telenomus sp, Trichograma chilonis by reducing the amount of broad-spectrum insecticides usage.
Promote ecological engineering in rice field to enhance natural enemies (promote more natural conditions and reduce human disturbance).
Place perching stands in field after transplanting for nesting insectivorous birds.
Monitoring: Monitor weekly from seedling to harvest for the presence of the insect and damage symptoms.
Look for egg masses on the rice leaves.
Look for dead heart (central tiller dries up and is easily pulled from the base) at vegetative stage.
Look for whitehead (emerging panicles are whitish and empty) at reproductive stage.
Consider direct control actions when 2-3 egg masses/m2, 10-15% dead heart at vegetative stage and 5% White head symptoms at reproductive stage.
Direct Control: Install pheromone traps at 5 per acre from planting.
Set up light traps (1/acre in the field).
Collection and destruction of moths by sweeping and burning.

Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, pre-harvest interval, max number of sprays, restricted re- entry interval.
